extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal financial assistance (elementary/secondary schools and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, campus administrators, legal counsel, and policymakers
extracted.subtask_short: Title IX reporting & confidential employee rules
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted standards govern employees' notification obligations, the definition and duties of confidential employees, notice requirements, and recipient obligations under 34 C.F.R. §106.44 (and related sections) in the Department's final Title IX rule preamble. Applies to how institutions must classify, train, notify, and handle disclosures of conduct that may constitute sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 1 employee notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any employee who is not a confidential employee and who either has authority to institute corrective measures on behalf of the recipient or has responsibility for administrative leadership, teaching, or advising in the recipient's education program or activity must notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Category 1 mirrors the reporting requirement for non-confidential employees in elementary and secondary schools because of the authority and leadership roles such employees hold. Determination whether an employee is Category 1 is fact-specific and rests on the recipient's own policies. This requirement aligns with the §106.30(a) definition of “actual knowledge” in the 2020 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category 2 employee options
rubrics_metrics.description: All other employees who are not confidential employees are required to either: notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part; or provide the contact information of the Title IX Coordinator and information about how to make a complaint of sex discrimination to any person who provides the employee with information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recipient has discretion to determine which of these two actions Category 2 employees must take or to leave the discretion to those employees. The Department clarified that this option requires only stating how to make a complaint; Category 2 employees are not required to explain grievance procedures or supportive measures themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to require all non-confidential employees to notify
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient has discretion to require all employees (other than confidential employees) to notify the Title IX Coordinator when the employee has information about conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This simpler approach may reduce confusion and ensure all employees know what to do; recipients may adopt either the two-category framework or blanket reporting for non-confidential employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: No distinction based on discloser's student/employee status
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification obligations under §106.44(c)(2) do not differ based on whether the employee is receiving information from a student or another employee; employees should follow the same actions regardless of the discloser's status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department determined this is simpler, easier to understand, and avoids confusion about altering actions based on the discloser's status. Recipients should not require employees to change response based on whether the person disclosing is a student or employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient determination of employee category (no job-title enumeration)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to enumerate all job titles covered; recipients must reasonably determine whether a particular employee is in Category 1 or Category 2 based on the facts and their policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should use a straightforward set of inquiries to determine Category 1 status (authority to institute corrective measures or responsibility for leadership/teaching/advising). Recipients must give notice to employees of which category applies and update determinations when duties change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training promptness and frequency for duty changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When an employee changes positions that alters their duties under Title IX or the final regulations, training must occur promptly and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This addresses employees with fluctuating duties who may move between Category 1 and Category 2 and ensures they receive updated training when their Title IX responsibilities change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential employee exemption from notification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator when a person informs them of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference to “advising” in §106.44(c)(2)(i) does not change the definition of confidential employee; an advisor who meets the definition of confidential employee is exempt. However, confidential employees remain subject to other applicable laws that may require reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient notice of confidential employees
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must notify all participants in its education program or activity of how to contact its confidential employees, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.44(d) requires recipients to publicize how to contact confidential employees, subject to limited exclusions discussed in the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures by confidential employees upon receiving a disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A confidential employee, in response to a person who informs that employee of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination, must: explain the employee's status as confidential for purposes of Title IX and the Title IX regulations, including circumstances in which the employee is not required to notify the Title IX Coordinator; provide that person with contact information for the Title IX Coordinator; explain how to make a complaint of sex discrimination; and explain that the Title IX Coordinator may be able to offer and coordinate supportive measures as well as initiate an informal resolution process or an investigation under the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures individuals accessing confidential services learn how to contact the Title IX Coordinator and understand the limits of confidentiality and available options without triggering a Title IX report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation of confidential status
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee's confidential status for purposes of the Title IX regulations is only with respect to information the employee receives while functioning within the scope of their duties to which privilege or confidentiality applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department revised the first category to state confidentiality is limited to information received while the employee is functioning within the scope of duties to which privilege or confidentiality applies, clarifying that communications may not be confidential for all purposes and only apply 'for purposes this part.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential resources vs confidential employees distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Confidential resource’ is not synonymous with ‘confidential employee.’ A confidential resource need not be an employee of the recipient and does not need to comply with the notification exception at §106.44(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should note that confidential resources (including non-employees) can be consulted without triggering Title IX reporting obligations, but only confidential employees (employees of the recipient meeting §106.2) are covered by the regulatory confidential-employee provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement to designate specific job types as confidential employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to designate specific types of individuals (e.g., teachers, victim advocates) as confidential employees in the regulations; recipients retain flexibility to designate confidential employees based on assigned duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorical designations could be inaccurate across diverse recipients. However, many suggested examples (e.g., victim advocates, counseling staff) are likely to qualify depending on duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with other Federal/State/local laws (reporting obligations remain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employee exceptions in §106.44(d) are limited to Title IX and do not exempt confidential employees from complying with obligations under other Federal, State, or local law to report sex discrimination, including sex-based harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section §106.44(j) generally prohibits disclosures of personally identifiable information obtained in complying with this part, but such disclosures are permissible if required by Federal law/regulations or if required/authorized by State law or FERPA. Recipients must comply with overlapping obligations (e.g., mandatory child abuse reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: No new Clery/EEOC/Title VII or VAWA alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: These Title IX regulations do not alter requirements under the Clery Act, Title VII, VAWA, or other Federal laws; recipients remain subject to those obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to opine on Clery Act disclosure responsibilities within these Title IX regulations and notes recipients must still comply with other statutory/regulatory regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety-threat reporting not imposed on confidential employees by rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require confidential employees to immediately report conduct that poses a safety threat; recipients may, however, require all non-confidential employees to report safety threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Federal, State, or local law requires a confidential employee to report safety threats (e.g., mandated reporting of sexual assault of a child), such disclosures are permissible under §106.44(j). Recipients may choose to require broader internal reporting of safety threats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination must include Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.8(c)(1)(i) requires that the name or title, office address, email address, and telephone number of the recipient's Title IX Coordinator be included in the recipient's notice of nondiscrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement supports access by students (including study abroad participants who return) to contact information needed to make complaints or obtain supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients must specify student-employee coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must reasonably determine and specify whether and under what circumstances a person who is both a student and an employee is subject to the requirements of paragraph (c)(2) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department removed proposed prescriptive factors and allowed recipients flexibility to consider factors (such as primary relationship or whether the disclosure occurred in employment context) but requires recipients to give notice to student-employees about the circumstances that apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee-complainant autonomy (notification exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this section do not apply to an employee who has personally been subject to conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination under Title IX or this part; an employee complainant's decision to notify is left to that employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an employee complainant tells another employee, that receiving employee retains notification obligations under §106.44(c)(1) and (2). The Department declined to adopt a rule that a recipient lacks notice if only the respondent has actual knowledge.
